subtype: Approach: drops a project that is not working after some effort [Thinking]
passage:
In the school craft room, Pradeep had been building a tall tower of ice-cream sticks for three afternoons. It kept leaning. Each time the top piece went on, the glue slipped. Pradeep held the wobbly tower and said out loud, "This glue is too slippery for so many sticks. If I add more days it will still fall."

Gurleen, the craft teacher, walked by and only asked, "What will you do?"

Pradeep took a breath. "I'll stop this one. I'll build a small hut instead, with only ten sticks, and use the strong paste from the shelf."

He put the tower gently in the box. By evening the hut stood by itself. It was small, but it did not lean.

qa.q: How many afternoons had Pradeep been building the tower?
qa.a: Pradeep had been building the tower for three afternoons.

qa.q: How was Pradeep feeling while holding the wobbly tower?
qa.a: Pradeep was frustrated and unsure, but thoughtful, saying that more days would not stop it falling.

qa.q: What could Pradeep try if the hut also leans?
qa.a: Pradeep could dry each layer before adding the next, or ask Gurleen which paste holds best.

qa.q: How might Gurleen see Pradeep's decision?
qa.a: Gurleen may feel pleased that Pradeep decided alone after being asked only one question.

grounding: Shows a boy dropping a big model when the glue will not hold and starting a smaller design instead of spending more days.

subtype: Approach: drops a project that is not working after some effort [Thinking]
passage: I'm Sonali, Sumit's big sister. For a whole week he'd been building a giant bridge out of ice-cream sticks for the school craft show, the biggest thing he'd ever made. It covered half the dining table. On Saturday I heard a crack and then silence. The middle had sagged again. Sumit pressed the sticks together and held them, counting. He let go. It sagged. He sat back and I heard him talking to himself. "This glue is too weak for something this long. If I keep adding more glue, it'll just get heavier and droop more." He looked at the calendar: four days left. Then he pulled out a fresh sheet and started drawing a much smaller bridge, with triangles in the sides.

qa.q: How many days were left before the craft show?
What does Sumit talking to himself suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: He seemed frustrated but thinking clearly, disappointed to give up the big bridge yet sure the glue wouldn't hold.

qa.q: What else could Sumit do to make the smaller bridge strong?
qa.a: Test the triangle shape on a small piece first, and ask a grown-up about stronger glue before the show.

qa.q: How might Sonali see her brother's decision?
qa.a: Sonali seems impressed that he stopped and started again rather than wasting four more days.

grounding: A boy stops building a big model after realising the glue will not hold and starts a smaller design instead.

subtype: Approach: drops a project that is not working after some effort [Thinking]
passage:
Sunday: Kamal began a huge cardboard ship with three decks for the science fair. He and his friend Hemant used a whole bottle of school glue.

Wednesday: The top deck kept sliding off. Kamal held it for five minutes, let go, and it slid again. The glue under it was still wet and soft. He sat on the floor and thought out loud. "Two more days of this and it'll still fall. The glue can't hold cardboard this heavy. I've spent three days, but the next three matter more." Hemant groaned. "All that work!"

Friday: On the table stood a small one-deck ship, with a little card sail. It was neat and dry. Kamal put the big broken ship by the door for recycling and smiled.

qa.q: What did Kamal and Hemant use for the ship?
qa.a: A whole bottle of school glue.

qa.q: How did Kamal feel on Wednesday when the deck slid again?
qa.a: He felt frustrated, but calm enough to think out loud and decide the next days mattered more than the ones spent.

qa.q: What small step helped Kamal most?
qa.a: Stopping to think out loud about the glue and the time left, then choosing a smaller design that could actually work.

qa.q: How does Hemant see giving up the big ship?
qa.a: Hemant is upset about losing all that work, though the neat ship on Friday may change his mind.

grounding: A boy stops building a big model when he sees the glue won't hold and makes a smaller design instead of wasting more days.
